chatter.ancientwarfare.priest.0: May the gods keep you, wanderer.
chatter.ancientwarfare.priest.2: Peace to this house and to you.
chatter.ancientwarfare.priest.3: Even a warrior needs comfort sometimes.
chatter.ancientwarfare.bard.0: Want a song about your deeds? If you have any.
chatter.ancientwarfare.bard.1: They threw turnips at me in the tavern yesterday. Success!
chatter.ancientwarfare.bard.2: My new song is almost done, I just need a rhyme.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.0: The neighbour's goat got into the garden again.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.2: My back aches. Rain's coming, I bet.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.3: They say wolves were seen in the woods.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.4: The smith raised his prices again.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.5: My son wants to be a soldier. Him, of all people...
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.6: The well needs cleaning, the water's muddy.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.7: Yesterday's sunset was a sight to see.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.8: So much work, and the day's so short.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.9: Did you see where the old miller went?
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.10: There was another fight at the tavern last night.
chatter.ancientwarfare.morning.1: Morning is the time for work.
chatter.ancientwarfare.morning.2: The roosters were screaming this morning.
chatter.ancientwarfare.morning.3: Fresh bread is in the oven already.
chatter.ancientwarfare.evening.0: Evening already. Time for a rest.
chatter.ancientwarfare.evening.1: Let's go to the square, people are there tonight.
chatter.ancientwarfare.evening.2: Another day gone, thank the gods.
chatter.ancientwarfare.evening.3: Supper's getting cold and here I am chatting.
chatter.ancientwarfare.night.0: Why aren't you asleep? It's night.
chatter.ancientwarfare.night.1: Better not go beyond the walls at night.
chatter.ancientwarfare.night.2: Hear that? Something's howling past the hill.
chatter.ancientwarfare.night.4: You'd want a torch. It's pitch dark.
chatter.ancientwarfare.rain.0: Pouring again! Good for the crops, at least.
chatter.ancientwarfare.rain.2: Weather like this is for sitting by the hearth.
chatter.ancientwarfare.rain.3: The roof is leaking again, curse it.
chatter.ancientwarfare.thunder.0: A storm! Don't stand under a tree!
chatter.ancientwarfare.winter.0: So cold. I hope the firewood lasts till spring.
chatter.ancientwarfare.winter.1: In winter bread is dearer and days are shorter.
chatter.ancientwarfare.winter.2: My fingers won't bend in this frost.
chatter.ancientwarfare.spring.1: The birds are back, hear them?
chatter.ancientwarfare.spring.2: The roads are all mud, the cart got stuck again.
chatter.ancientwarfare.summer.0: It's so hot the hens won't lay.
chatter.ancientwarfare.summer.1: The wheat looks good this year, touch wood.
chatter.ancientwarfare.summer.2: I'd go for a swim, but work won't wait.
chatter.ancientwarfare.autumn.0: The harvest is in, now we can celebrate.
chatter.ancientwarfare.autumn.1: The barns are full, we'll last the winter.
chatter.ancientwarfare.autumn.2: Leaves are falling, the cold is coming.
chatter.ancientwarfare.autumn.3: So many apples this year, more than we need.
chatter.ancientwarfare.famine.0: There's no bread at all. Nothing to feed the children.
chatter.ancientwarfare.famine.1: Would you have a little food to spare?
chatter.ancientwarfare.famine.3: Another week of hunger like this and people will flee.
chatter.ancientwarfare.plague.0: Don't come close, there's sickness here.
chatter.ancientwarfare.plague.1: A third house boarded up this week...
chatter.ancientwarfare.plague.2: The healer is run off his feet.
chatter.ancientwarfare.market.0: It's market day! Hurry before it's all gone.
chatter.ancientwarfare.market.1: So many people, you can't get through.
chatter.ancientwarfare.market.2: Bought cloth for my wife, now my purse is empty.
chatter.ancientwarfare.market.3: The visiting traders are generous today.
chatter.ancientwarfare.festival.0: A feast! Eat, drink and be merry!
chatter.ancientwarfare.festival.1: There'll be lights in the sky tonight, don't miss them.
chatter.ancientwarfare.festival.3: We haven't celebrated like this in ages.
chatter.ancientwarfare.war.0: They say %s are coming for us again.
chatter.ancientwarfare.war.1: War with %s. My brother marched with the army.
chatter.ancientwarfare.war.3: While the war with %s lasts, we sleep with one eye open.
chatter.ancientwarfare.grown.0: Seen the new house on the edge of town? We're growing!
chatter.ancientwarfare.grown.1: Soon our village will be a town.
chatter.ancientwarfare.grown.2: New neighbours moved in, good people.
chatter.ancientwarfare.wounded.0: You're covered in blood! Sit down, rest.
chatter.ancientwarfare.wounded.1: You need a healer, and quickly.
chatter.ancientwarfare.weapon.0: Put that weapon away, these are peaceful folk.
chatter.ancientwarfare.weapon.1: Don't wave that sword about in the street.
chatter.ancientwarfare.weapon.2: Sharp blade you have there. Not for us, I hope.
chatter.ancientwarfare.sneak.2: We don't like thieves here, mind you.
chatter.ancientwarfare.riding.0: Fine horse! Want to sell it?
chatter.ancientwarfare.riding.1: Slow down, there are children about!
chatter.ancientwarfare.country.0: You're the ruler of %s, aren't you? They say it's well run.
chatter.ancientwarfare.country.1: I've heard of %s. Maybe I should move there...
chatter.ancientwarfare.country.2: The ruler of %s, here! What an honour.
chatter.ancientwarfare.helper.0: Thanks for answering our notice board.
chatter.ancientwarfare.helper.1: You took on our task, didn't you? We're counting on you.
chatter.ancientwarfare.helper.2: They say you do the tasks from the board. Well done.
chatter.ancientwarfare.break.0: Hey! Don't break that, it's ours!
chatter.ancientwarfare.break.2: Who's going to fix that, you?
chatter.ancientwarfare.thanks.0: Thank you! May the gods keep you.
chatter.ancientwarfare.dialog.0.a: Did you hear the smith is getting married?
chatter.ancientwarfare.dialog.2.a: Your goat ate my garden again!
chatter.ancientwarfare.dialog.2.b: That's not my goat, I swear!
chatter.ancientwarfare.dialog.4.a: Seen how many guards there are today?
chatter.ancientwarfare.dialog.5.a: They say gold was found in the hills.
chatter.ancientwarfare.dialog.5.b: They say a lot. Get back to work.
chatter.ancientwarfare.dialog.6.b: We should stock up on firewood.
chatter.ancientwarfare.dialog.7.a: Your boy climbed the roof again.
chatter.ancientwarfare.dialog.8.a: What do they charge for bread now?
chatter.ancientwarfare.dialog.8.b: Three times too much, as always.
chatter.ancientwarfare.dialog.9.a: Did you hear that noise last night?

rumour.ancientwarfare.small_talk.6: My knee aches. Rain's coming, mark my words.
rumour.ancientwarfare.small_talk.7: The cow's gone dry three days now. Someone's put the evil eye on her.
rumour.ancientwarfare.small_talk.8: My neighbour moved his fence again. A whole cubit onto my land!
rumour.ancientwarfare.small_talk.9: A fox took a hen last night. I ought to get a dog.
rumour.ancientwarfare.small_talk.10: The miller's short-weighting the flour again. Everyone knows it.
rumour.ancientwarfare.small_talk.11: My daughter wants to marry, and there's no dowry to give.
rumour.ancientwarfare.small_talk.12: My teeth ache since morning. Old age, I suppose.
rumour.ancientwarfare.small_talk.13: There's chaff in the bread this year, but bread's bread.
rumour.ancientwarfare.small_talk.14: My eldest wants to be a soldier. The fool.
rumour.ancientwarfare.small_talk.15: Hard winter coming, they say. The geese left early.
rumour.ancientwarfare.small_talk.16: The roof leaks and there's nobody to mend it.
rumour.ancientwarfare.small_talk.17: Another brawl at the inn last night. Over a girl, they say.
rumour.ancientwarfare.small_talk.18: My boots are worn through, and the cobbler wants a fortune.
rumour.ancientwarfare.small_talk.19: My aunt knows her herbs. If you fall ill, call on her.
chatter.ancientwarfare.theft.1: Hey! Put that back, it's not yours!
chatter.ancientwarfare.theft.3: I saw that! Shame on you!
chatter.ancientwarfare.bed.0: Out of my bed, you lout!
chatter.ancientwarfare.bed.1: Who let you in? Get out!
chatter.ancientwarfare.bed.2: This is no inn! Go pay for a room!

crime.ancientwarfare.bed: This bed belongs to someone. A room can be had at the tavern.

chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.12: The bread came out burnt again. Third time this week.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.13: My knees creak louder than the old gate.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.14: Has anyone seen my good knife? The one with the bone handle.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.15: The miller swears the wheel turns slower on feast days.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.16: If the hens stop laying, it's that fox again.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.17: I traded two eggs for a ribbon. Worth it.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.18: The roof leaks right over my bed. Of course it does.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.19: Somebody keeps borrowing my bucket and never returns it.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.20: My grandmother says the winters were harder in her day.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.21: The children found a frog and named it after the lord.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.22: The baker's wife knows everything before it happens.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.23: A cart lost a wheel by the gate. Took half the morning to clear.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.24: I dreamt of fish all night. Must mean something.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.25: Don't drink from the trough, whatever the boys tell you.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.26: The new well bucket is twice the weight of the old one.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.27: I've patched these boots so often there's no boot left.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.28: My cousin went to the capital and came back with airs.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.29: The cat caught a rat bigger than itself. Proud as a knight.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.30: Somebody's been picking my apples before they're ripe.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.31: The bells woke me before the rooster did.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.32: Wool's cheap this year. Too many sheep, not enough hands.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.33: I swept the doorstep and the wind put it all back.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.34: The old soldier tells the same story every evening. It grows each time.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.35: I'd give a silver coin for a proper night's sleep.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.36: The goat ate my hat. My good hat.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.37: My neighbour's dog howls whenever the bard plays.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.38: Smoke's going straight up today. Good weather coming.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.39: They say a traveller paid for his ale with a pearl.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.40: I need more thread. And more patience.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.41: The pigs got out again. The whole street was chasing them.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.42: Mind the puddle by the smithy. It's deeper than it looks.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.43: My daughter wants to marry the cooper's boy. Could be worse.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.44: The cheese is ready. Smells like the whole valley.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.45: I counted the sheep twice and got two different numbers.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.46: Someone carved their name into the tavern table. Badly.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.47: The stew needs salt, and salt costs too much.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.48: Nothing ever happens here. And thank the gods for that.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.49: Firewood's damp. We'll be coughing all evening.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.50: The weaver finished the tapestry. Took her two winters.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.51: I found a coin in the mud this morning. Lucky day.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.52: The ox refuses to work past noon. Smart animal.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.53: Every time I sit down someone needs me.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.54: The herbs by the wall are good for a sore throat.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.55: My husband snores like a war horn.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.56: Did you hear the owl last night? Three times it called.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.57: The youngsters are courting by the well again.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.58: A peddler sold me a cure for baldness. Still bald.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.59: The road is all ruts after the rain.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.60: I mended the fence. The cow broke it by supper.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.61: Honey's sweet this year. The bees must be happy.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.62: I hope the harvest holds. We can't afford another bad year.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.63: The tanner's yard stinks worse every day.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.64: Some say the old tower is haunted. I say it's bats.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.65: If you're going to the market, bring me back onions.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.66: The priest's sermon was long, but the bread after was good.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.67: My boy carved a wooden sword. Now he fights the chickens.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.68: The wind took my washing clear over the wall.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.69: I keep meaning to fix that shutter.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.70: The carpenter's apprentice hit his thumb again. We all heard.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.71: A good pair of boots outlasts a bad king, my father said.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.72: The river's low. The fish are lazy.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.73: I sold the spotted calf. Already miss the little beast.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.74: Watch your purse in the crowd. Quick fingers about.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.75: The guard at the gate fell asleep on his spear again.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.76: Too hot to work, too poor not to.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.77: They're digging a new ditch. Nobody knows what for.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.78: My hands smell of onions and they always will.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.79: The old woman by the mill reads fortunes in beans.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.80: I lent my ladder and now I'm the one who has to ask for it.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.81: Fresh straw in the beds tonight. Small joys.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.82: They raised the toll on the bridge. Again.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.83: The candle-maker's out of wax. Dark evenings ahead.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.84: The little ones are playing at war again. I don't like it.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.85: I could eat a whole roast goose by myself today.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.86: Who left the gate to the pen open? Who?
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.87: A stranger asked the way to the capital. I sent him the long way.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.88: The tavern keeper waters the ale. Everybody knows.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.89: Hard work never killed anyone, but I won't be the first to try.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.90: The moon was red last night. My mother would have worried.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.91: Found a horseshoe on the road. Nailed it over the door.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.92: I've walked to the field and back twice. Forgot the hoe both times.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.93: The bread's fresh at the baker's. Go before it's gone.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.94: Somebody's whistling the same tune all day. It's in my head now.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.95: Don't stand there, the cart's coming through!
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.96: I'll rest when I'm old. Oh wait.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.97: The flowers by the shrine came up early this year.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.98: Mud everywhere. Mud in my soup, I swear.
chatter.ancientwarfare.idle.99: A good day. Nobody quarrelled, nobody died.
chatter.ancientwarfare.dear.0: %s costs a fortune here now. Nobody brings any.
chatter.ancientwarfare.dear.2: If you have %s to sell, the traders will pay well.
chatter.ancientwarfare.dear.3: We're short of it again. %s, I mean.
chatter.ancientwarfare.dear.4: The caravans haven't brought %s in days.
chatter.ancientwarfare.dear.5: %s is worth its weight in silver this week.
chatter.ancientwarfare.cheap.0: %s is cheap as dirt here. Everybody has too much.
chatter.ancientwarfare.cheap.1: Buy %s here, you won't find it cheaper anywhere.
chatter.ancientwarfare.cheap.2: We can't give %s away, the stores are full.
chatter.ancientwarfare.cheap.3: Another cart of it came in. %s, as always.
